raw.assessment: The incumbent provides an assembly-stage opportunity to check parts and fit, with no recorded damage claims (O7), but median time is 11 minutes (O2) and unaided arrangement succeeds for only seven of ten observed customers (O4). Five content-error reports (O3) warrant investigation; they do not establish five independently verified omissions. O6 is a concrete limit on a universal assembly-speed explanation: both workers achieve seven to nine minutes on repeated three-compartment orders, while all extreme delays occur in mixed batches. Layout complexity and switching remain confounded. O5 also limits a simple partition-width explanation because measured widths overlap across successful and retried insertions.

openings.claim: Order-specific staged kits with a layout-and-color contents check may reduce selection/checking delays and content errors caused by shared-bin selection or order switching.
openings.delta: Locate a potentially avoidable part of the incumbent's delay before changing partition geometry or transferring assembly to customers.
openings.prediction: Within the same layout, staged kits reduce total selection-plus-checking time, including kit preparation, and independently observed contents discrepancies; insertion time changes little.
openings.probe: Use 12 sample builds: each worker performs each of the three layouts once per method, with order counterbalanced. Record selection, insertion, checking, packing and kit preparation separately; independently reconcile parts against the order. Include uncommon-color orders. Record setup cost and preparation time before adoption.
assumptions: Reusable staging fits the single bench and initial budget.
Preparation does not jeopardize the fixed delivery date; recurring material stays within 0.40.
Ordered counts, colors, footprint, capacity and removable partitions remain intact.

openings.claim: An order-specific diagram highlighting the short partition's location may improve unaided arrangement success.
openings.delta: Test layout recognition as a failure source independently of missing components or insertion difficulty.
openings.prediction: With verified complete, identical kits, the revised diagram reduces short-partition questions and increases correct unaided arrangements.
openings.probe: Randomly assign five participants to each diagram version using the same ordered layout. Record correct arrangement, help requests and time within ten minutes. Treat this small comparison as directional evidence, not proof of the 90% pilot target.
assumptions: Diagram preparation and printing fit the shared budget and fixed schedule.
Partitions remain removable and the supplied physical product is unchanged.

raw.assessment: Two testable substitutions; neither is established by the observations. Combined timing obscures the achievable saving. Preserve every accepted layout and exterior color, the footprint, assortment, rearrangeability, budget and delivery date; small samples cannot establish the 60-order success measures.

openings.claim: Hypothesis: an order-specific flat-pack carrier could perform component accounting and placement guidance. Each required partition occupies a labeled silhouette; matching removable labels identify its destination on the ordered-layout diagram. Empty silhouettes expose omissions, while the diagram directs customer assembly, including the short partition.
openings.delta: Moves completeness checking into the packing artifact and initial assembly from workshop labor to an artifact-guided customer action; fully assembled dispatch is a changeable assumption.
openings.prediction: If the carrier works, deliberate omissions are detected before closure, customer short-partition errors decrease, and workshop time falls without reducing completed-layout success.
openings.probe: Use six spare-board samples across ordered compartment counts and colors. Test seeded missing/wrong pieces, then ten participants assembling without help. Record selection, checking and packing times separately, final fit and assortment capacity, and transport protection. Price the carrier and preparation time before any order change.
assumptions: Carrier contents and diagram are generated correctly from each order.
Packaging changes stay within both cost limits and the fixed delivery date.

openings.claim: Short tapered lead-ins on partition tabs might transfer insertion alignment from repeated hand adjustment into the tab geometry, retaining the original seated engagement surfaces and removable joint.
openings.delta: The material guides initial entry; overlapping recorded widths do not establish whether alignment causes retries.
openings.prediction: Alignment-driven retries should decline with tapered entry, including among parts with overlapping widths; unchanged retries weaken this explanation.
openings.probe: Use six modified samples and three unchanged controls. Counterbalance insertion order across workers and participants; record retries and insertion time separately. Check retention under the specified assortment and repeated dismantling. Adopt only if template work fits the budget and delivery date.
assumptions: Existing templates permit a short lead-in without weakening seated joints.
Insertion savings materially affect total workshop time.

openings.claim: Order-specific staging may reduce selection delays and content errors.
openings.probe: Twelve counterbalanced builds; time stages including preparation; audit contents/colors and bench space.

openings.claim: Ordered-layout diagrams may clarify short-partition placement.
openings.probe: Randomize ten participants, five per diagram; record unaided arrangement, questions and time.

openings.claim: Labeled silhouette carriers may check completeness and guide customer assembly, replacing workshop assembly.
openings.discriminator: Seeded errors detected; workshop time falls with successful customer layouts.
openings.probe: Six samples spanning counts/colors; seed missing/wrong parts; ten unaided users; time stages, check capacity/protection and price carrier/preparation.
openings.uncertainty: Order mapping and transport protection unverified.

openings.claim: Tapered tab entries may reduce alignment retries while preserving seated engagement.
openings.probe: Six modified/three controls; counterbalance insertions; time retries; check loaded retention and repeated dismantling.
openings.uncertainty: Alignment cause, strength and total-time savings unproven.

post_distill.decision: Retain four hypotheses. Adoption requires 30x20 cm footprint, original assortment, removable partitions, selected counts/colors, fixed delivery, setup <=500 and recurring increment <=0.40. Schedule within 15 samples/ten participants. Small probes cannot establish 60-unit targets: >=98% complete, median <=8 minutes, >=90% unaided.
